why_showable: Real product — live demo verified at https://www.aryanbloodbank.org/. Substantial TypeScript frontend and backend code (e.g. package.json, bloodlink/src/main.tsx, bloodlink/supabase/functions/_shared/otpDelivery.ts) and an internal audit document (bloodlink/docs/BLOODLINK_FULL_AUDIT_2026-08-02.md) support a genuine effort, not a toy repo.
strengths: Full-stack app with real features: React/Vite frontend (bloodlink/vite.config.ts, bloodlink/src/...), Supabase Edge Functions (bloodlink/supabase/functions/kyc-otp/index.ts), KYC/OTP, geocoding and analytics code.
Good separation and TypeScript usage: contexts, hooks, services, and security modules (security/*.ts).
Live demo + audit doc increase credibility.
weaknesses: Sparse automated coverage: dossier shows 249 source / 1 test and top-level package.json has empty scripts — minimal tests and NO CI (blocker: no_ci).
Missing governance: no license, thin README, no topics — hurts reuse/hiring claims.

Risky runtime defaults: permissive dev CORS and env-driven dev OTP (bloodlink/supabase/functions/_shared/otpDelivery.ts) can leak OTPs if misconfigured. Several functions throw on missing env — brittle deploy UX.
review:
Codebase is well-organized and production-minded: supabase helpers, sanitize/rateLimit/sessionManager modules show security thinking. However, hard-coded dev-fallbacks and env-dependent guards need tightening: require safe defaults, fail-closed for OTP/CORS, and remove DEV_RETURN_OTP from production. Add CI (lint, build, test), expand tests, add a clear CONTRIBUTING/license, and run secret-scans before claiming showable. Paths to inspect first: package.json, bloodlink/src/main.tsx, bloodlink/supabase/functions/_shared/otpDelivery.ts.

_Cited:_ package.json, bloodlink/src/main.tsx, bloodlink/supabase/functions/_shared/otpDelivery.ts, bloodlink/docs/BLOODLINK_FULL_AUDIT_2026-08-02.md, bloodlink/vite.config.ts, bloodlink/supabase/functions/kyc-otp/index.ts
